riddles.question: What has four fingers and a thumb, but is not living?
hints: You wear a pair of these outside in the winter.
They keep your hands warm.
They have separate slots for your fingers.

riddles.question: What has hands but cannot clap? A face but cannot smile?
hints: It helps you keep track of time during the day.
You might hear it ticking on the living room wall.
It often sits on a bedside table.

riddles.question: They come out at night without being called, and are lost in the day without being stolen. What are they?
hints: You look up at the night sky to see them.
They twinkle far out in space.
They disappear when the sun comes up.

riddles.question: What is always in front of you, but can’t be seen?
hints: It hasn't happened yet.
Tomorrow is a part of it.
You walk toward it every single day.

riddles.question: It has keys, but no locks. It has space, but no room. You can enter, but can’t go inside. What is it?
hints: You use it when typing on a computer.
It features a spacebar and letters from A to Z.
It helps you communicate on a desktop or laptop.

riddles.question: What has many rings but no fingers?
hints: It makes a ringing sound when someone calls you.
Most people carry one around in their pocket or purse.
You use it to talk to family and friends.

riddles.question: What can you break without touching it?
hints: It involves a spoken agreement or your word.
Breaking it can hurt someone's trust.
It is made with a statement like 'I swear I will do this.'

riddles.question: David’s father has three sons: Snap, Crackle and _____?
hints: Don't let the cereal characters trick you.
Read the very first word of the question again.
The father belongs to someone named...

riddles.question: I’m not a blanket, yet I cover the ground. What am I?
hints: It falls from the clouds during cold winter months.
It is white, cold, and can be shoveled off a driveway.
Children love to use it to build snowmen.

riddles.question: I get wetter the more I dry. What am I?
hints: You keep one hanging in the bathroom.
You use it to dry off after stepping out of the shower.
It soaks up water from your skin.

riddles.question: The more you take from me, the bigger I become. What am I?
hints: Think about gardening or landscaping work.
You dig it into the dirt or ground.
The more earth you scoop out, the larger it gets.

riddles.question: I have one eye but cannot see. What am I?
hints: It is very thin and made of metal.
It is used alongside thread for sewing clothes or buttons.
You have to be careful not to poke your finger with its sharp tip.

riddles.question: You can catch me, but you cannot throw me. What am I?
hints: It is a common mild illness that brings a runny nose or cough.
You might catch it from someone sneezing nearby during winter.
It usually clears up after a week of rest.

riddles.question: I travel all around the world but stay in one corner. What am I?
hints: You need it to mail a traditional paper letter.
You moisten the back or peel it to stick it down.
It always goes in the top right part of an envelope.

riddles.question: The more I have, the less you see. I am…
hints: It happens naturally every night when the sun goes down.
You experience it when you turn off all the bedside lamps.
It makes it hard to read a book without a light on.

riddles.question: I follow you during the day but disappear at night. What am I?
hints: It is created on the ground when you block the sunlight.
It mimics your movements as you walk outside.
When the sun goes away, it vanishes too.

riddles.question: You use me to unlock knowledge instead of doors
hints: It has a front cover, a back cover, and many paper pages.
You might read one by your favorite author in an armchair.
It can take you on an adventure or teach you history.

riddles.question: What has a head but no brain
hints: You buy it at the grocery store produce section.
It is leafy, green, and crisp.
It is the main ingredient in a garden salad.

riddles.question: I have a neck but no head, I have two arms, but no hands. What am I?
hints: It is a common item found in your closet or dresser drawer.
You put it on your upper body every morning.
It has sleeves that cover your arms.

riddles.question: What gets smaller every time it takes a bath?
hints: You keep it by the sink or in the shower.
It creates lather and bubbles to clean your hands.
Over weeks of washing, the bar slowly wears away.
